transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um... well, I guess what brings me in is that I’ve been feeling like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. I teach special education, so, you know, having a lot of energy is usually a good thing, right? It helps me keep up with the kids. But... well, lately I just finish one thing at school, or even when I get home, and I immediately jump right into the next project. It's like I'm never really able to just shut myself off. 

I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about being productive, because I know working hard is a good trait to have, but it's just gotten a little exhausting to be on the go all the time. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Have you been sleeping less than usual lately, or finding that you don’t really need as much sleep as you used to?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I definitely still need my sleep. Um... I try to be really responsible about my bedtime, actually, because I know how important rest is to be at my best for the students. 

I mean, sometimes I might stay up a little late because I'm just... well, still going on a project and have a hard time stopping, but I definitely feel it the next day. I haven't noticed that I can just get by on less sleep at all. I'm not one of those people who can survive on three hours. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed yourself talking more quickly or feeling like you need to keep talking, maybe even interrupting others because your thoughts are moving so fast?

Well, um... I guess I do talk a bit, but I really just want to make sure I'm being thorough, you know? Communication is so important in my job. 

But... I suppose I might get a little carried away sometimes. Like, I’ll go into a parent conference or a staff meeting, and I'll tell myself I'm just going to give a quick update. But then... well, then I hear myself giving three different examples, and then a story from my classroom, and then maybe some extra ideas that nobody really asked for. And I can tell the other person is clearly trying to wrap it up, but I just... keep going. 

I don't mean to be overbearing, I really don't. I just want to be helpful and make sure everyone has all the details. Is that a bad thing? I hope I'm not coming across as too much.
Have you noticed your thoughts racing or jumping from one idea to another quickly, even when you're trying to focus on just one thing?

No, I wouldn't say my thoughts are racing. I mean, as a teacher, you kind of have to be able to juggle a lot of different things at once, right? You're thinking about the lesson plan, the student who needs extra help, the paperwork... so my mind is definitely active. 

But I don't feel like my thoughts are out of control or jumping around wildly. I just like to make connections and think things through from a few different angles to make sure I'm doing the best job I can. I really try to stay focused on what's important. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just don't think "racing" is the right word for it. Does that sound okay?
Have you noticed yourself becoming more restless or needing to keep moving, like you can't sit still for very long, even when you want to?

Well, um... I guess I do have a hard time just... sitting perfectly still sometimes. But I think that's pretty normal, right? I mean, sitting for long stretches can be tough for anyone. 

I try really hard to be professional, especially when I'm in IEP meetings with parents or taking my admin classes. I know it's important to look attentive. But... I suppose I do get a little fidgety. Like, my leg will be bouncing under the table, or I'll be clicking a pen, or just shifting around in my chair a lot. 

To be honest, sometimes I don't even realize I'm doing it until I see someone glance over at me. Then I feel terrible and try to freeze, because I don't want them to think I'm not listening or that I'm bored. I really am paying attention! I just... I guess my body just wants to be doing something. 

Is that a big problem? I hope I'm not being disruptive to the people around me. I really do try my best to keep it under control.
Have you found yourself starting more projects than usual, or doing things more energetically than before, like you can't slow yourself down even if you want to?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any big changes in my energy levels or anything like that. 

I mean, I always have a few things going on, just with the nature of special ed and trying to keep my classroom running smoothly, but it's really just my normal routine. I wouldn't say I'm starting a bunch of new projects out of nowhere or acting more energetic than usual. I really try to just stay dependable and pace myself so I can be a stable presence for my students. 

I definitely don't feel like I can't slow down... I just like being productive and doing my job well. Is that what you were asking? I hope that's the kind of information you need.
Have you had any periods where you felt down, depressed, or hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even if it was just for a few days?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, everybody gets a little tired or has a rough day sometimes, especially in education, right? But feeling depressed or hopeless? No, definitely not. 

I really try to keep a positive outlook on things. My students rely on me to be a sort of cheerleader for them, so I always try to bring a good, upbeat attitude to the classroom. I wouldn't want to bring any negativity into their day. And I still really enjoy my work and the things I do on the weekends. 

I just try to focus on the good things and keep moving forward. I hope that's a good thing? I just really try not to let things get me down. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?

Have you had any periods where you felt unusually high-spirited, overly confident, or irritable — like you were on top of the world or needed to keep going without slowing down, even if others noticed it?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I've ever felt like that. I mean, I try to be confident in my teaching, just so the kids feel secure, but... definitely not overly confident or thinking I'm on top of the world. That sounds a bit arrogant, and I really try hard to be humble and easy to work with. 

And irritable? Well, um, I guess everyone has moments of frustration, but I really, really try to keep that in check. I'd feel awful if I ever snapped at anyone, especially my students or their parents. I just try to be a steady, supportive guy for everyone around me. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. I'm definitely just... pretty even-keeled in that regard, I think. Is that what you were looking for?
Have you ever noticed that you actually need less sleep than usual, not just that you're staying up later because you're busy or excited?

Oh, no... I don't think I've ever experienced that. I really need my sleep, to be honest. 

I mean, working in special ed, you really have to be alert and ready for anything, so I try to be very responsible about getting a good night's rest. I'd feel terrible if I came in exhausted and couldn't give the kids my best, you know? I really pride myself on being present for them. 

So, no, I definitely never feel like I can just get by on less sleep or anything like that. I always try to get a solid night's sleep so I can be dependable the next morning. Is that... is that what you were hoping to hear? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you found yourself getting easily distracted by things around you, even when you're trying to focus on something important?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I try very hard to stay focused, especially when I'm working with my students. They need me to be present, and I would hate to let them down by not paying attention. 

I suppose everyone's mind wanders a little bit here and there, right? Like if there's a loud noise in the hallway or something, but I always make sure to bring my attention right back to what I'm doing. I'm very dedicated to my job and to making sure I'm doing things right. 

I definitely don't let myself get easily distracted from important things. I really try to be as professional and attentive as possible. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering correctly.
Have you found yourself working on tasks or projects with more intensity or speed than usual, even if you weren’t necessarily starting new projects?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I try to work hard, of course, because my students really rely on me to have everything prepared for them. But I definitely don't rush through things or work with, you know, unusual intensity. 

I think rushing just leads to mistakes, and I'd feel just awful if I messed up a lesson plan or an IEP report because I was going too fast. I really try to be thorough and take my time to make sure everything is done carefully and correctly. I want to be someone my colleagues and the parents can count on.

So, no, I just try to keep a steady, reliable pace. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way. Is that the kind of answer you needed?

Have there ever been a time when you felt your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable for several days in a row, along with a big increase in your energy or activity level that felt different from your usual self?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I really strive to keep my mood, um, very even and predictable. 

You know, the students really pick up on your energy, so if I were unusually high-strung or... heaven forbid, irritable for days at a time, it would just completely disrupt their routine. I would never want to do that. I always try to be a calming, positive presence for them, because that's what they really need from me. 

So, no, I haven't ever felt out of control with my mood or had a big spike in energy like that. I just try to be my usual, steady self every single day. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful with these answers, I just really want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
